abstract: In 5G networks, a network slice is an independent end-to-end logical network running on a shared physical infrastructure, capable of guaranteeing a negotiated service level agreement (SLA) to deliver customized service. An end-to-end network slice includes three logical networks in the subnets: an access network (AN) sub-slice, a transport network (TN) sub-slice and a core network (CN) sub-slice. The network slice SLA needs to be decomposed into the corresponding sub-slice SLAs. In this paper, the SLA decomposition for network slicing is modelled as a constrained optimization problem and solved in two steps: building the sub-slice SLA acceptance probability models and solving the constrained optimization problem. The sub-slice SLA acceptance probability models are built by a self-attention convolutional neural network, and the constrained optimization problem is solved by a differential evolution algorithm based on the optimal acceptance probability of the SLA decomposition for network slicing. The simulation results show that the proposed self-attention convolutional neural network-based sub-slice SLA acceptance probability models (SACNN-SSAPMs) fit better with the ground truths, and the errors between the optimal acceptance probabilities of the SLA decomposition for network slicing based on the SACNN-SSAPMs and those based on the ground truths are smaller.

articleTitle: Prediction of FPSO single point mooring line tension based on Bayesian optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Oil exploitation requires offshore engineering equipment such as offshore platforms, positioning systems and drilling risers. As one of the positioning systems, the mechanical safety performance of mooring system is of great significance to offshore platforms. To ensure the safety of the mooring system under unknown sea conditions, predictive monitoring of mooring line tension magnitude is necessary. This paper uses business software Orcaflex to establish the single point mooring system model of FPSO, and then gives a mooring tension prediction method based on Training-data-set. The long short-term memory artificial neural network model is employed to establish the mooring line tension prediction model based on the parameters of the Bayesian optimization neural network model. The error analysis of the prediction results provides a valuable reference for the mooring system design.

articleTitle: Rail track curve recognition model based on PSO-LSTM algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In this study, a PSO-LSTM model is proposed<sup>[1]</sup>to increase the accuracy of rail curve detection. In order to alter the model's parameters, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) techniques are used to enhance the hidden layer and learning rate of the long-and-short-term memory neural network (LSTM). Afterward, apply the PSO-LSTM model to determine the rail's curvature. To make up the identifying process: Data processing, PSO algorithm optimization, and PSO-LSTM model prediction are the three steps. The PSO-LSTM<sup>[2]</sup>model is validated using data from train tracks, and it is contrasted with the Back Propagation(Bp)<sup>[3]</sup>and conventional LSTM<sup>[4]</sup>models. The outcomes demonstrate the superior accuracy and stability of the PSO-LSTM model.

Author Keywords: long and short-term memory neural network

articleTitle: Service Resilience Optimization Algorithm for Intelligent Space-based System with Minimum Delay
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Space-based systems have enormous economic, social and military values that make them vulnerable to interference and even attack. With the gradual development of networked and intelligent space-based systems, intelligent space-based systems can still maintain a certain service performance without paralysis when confronted with interference or attack, that is, flexible services. However, when a traditional space-based system encounters node failure, the service is directly interrupted or needs ground re-planning, and it does not have the ability of flexible service. To solve this problem, this paper presents a service resilience recovery algorithm for minimum latency. Experiments show that in the service elasticity evaluation of smart space-based systems based on real networks, the more satellite nodes there are, the better the service elasticity, and the recovery time is 42.3% shorter than the traditional random algorithm, which is 3 times higher than the nearest strategy.

articleTitle: A Novel Transmitarray Using Double-layer Hexagonal Element with Vias
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: A novel transmitarray using double-layer element with metal vias is proposed. Two hexagonal patches with similar characteruistics are etched on two sides of the single-layer substrate. Metal vias is used to improve the coupling strength and decrease the transmission loss. The proposed element and the transmitarray are simulated by Ansoft HFSS. Simulations show that the element has wide phase range of over 380 degrees. The transmission loss is above -2 dB at the center frequency of 12 GHz. The designed element shows potential in improving phase range. A square low-profile transmitarray is designed by using the proposed hexagonal element. Simulation result shows that the designed transmitarray antenna has 1-db gain bandwidth of 6.6% at 12 GHz.

articleTitle: Enhanced Module design based on ShuffleNetV2
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Among the general lightweight deep neural network models, ShuffleNetV2 is a portable and efficient model. To further make the network lighter and more powerful in recognition, an Enhanced Shuffle Block (ESBlock) is proposed, which is a symmetric module consisting of a depth-wise separable convolutional superposition to replace ShuffleNetV2's fundamental module. Then, by re-optimizing the configuration of channels, the expansion factor within the basic block, the layer of each stage, it is possible to improve the performance. And a Portable Attention Module (PAM) is added to enhance feature extraction and model's utilization capability. Experimental findings demonstrate that the enhanced network accomplishes 94.15% and 73.52% recognition accuracy on Cifar10 and Cifar100 datasets with only 0.66 M and 0.77 M parameters, respectively. Compared with the ShuffleNetV2, the accuracy is increased by 1% and 0.75%, and parameters is decreased by 50% and 44% respectively.

articleTitle: A Novel Two-Stage Net for Human Body Region Segmentation via Centimeter-Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Human body region segmentation is a sub-task in semantic segmentation. Due to the size, complexity, abstraction of radar signal and the lack of open source datasets of radar signal data, the radar signal is rarely used for human body segmentation in past. In recent years, with the development of deep learning, some radar signal data from unmanned drive has been used for research on classification, target detection and semantic segmentation. In this paper, a novel two-stage neural network model based on centimeter-wave radar sensor is designed for human body region segmentation. In the first stage, radar signals are encoded and compressed, in the second stage, decode the spatial feature information of the human body extracted by the encoder to output the segmentation results. The network adopts the design idea of teacher-student network, which use the teacher network to annotate radar signal data and provide cross-modal supervision for the student network. We collected human body data in different scenes, and input the radar signal into the model, performs human body region segmentation. The effectiveness of this human segmentation model is experimentally verified for single and multi-person scenes, especially for occlusion scenes.

articleTitle: Fractional Fourier Transform Based Channel Estimation in XL-MIMO systems
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) is a promising technology for current 5G communications, which can improve the spectral efficiency through beamforming or multiplexing. For future 6G communications, XL-MIMO has been proposed, which has much more antenna numbers than massive MIMO. With the increasement of antenna numbers, the spatial non-stationary effect becomes more obvious, which means different parts of the antenna see totally different scatterers. Traditional channel estimation schemes imply the spatial stationary assumption. Therefore, if traditional channel estimation schemes are utilized, the accuracy of channel estimation will decrease a lot. In this paper, we propose a fractional fourier transform (FrFT) based channel estimation scheme. This scheme can accurately estimate the spatial non-stationary channel. Specifically, the channel estimation scheme is divided into two steps. In the first step, the whole antenna is divided into several sub-arrays. In the second step, the channel corresponding to each sub-array is estimated based on the FrFT. Simulation results reveal that the proposed FrFT based channel estimation schemes has a better NMSE performance than the existing schemes.

articleTitle: Subspace-based Optimization Method with Adaptive Total Variation for Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Microwave imaging problems are nonlinear and ill-posed due to multiple scattering and a lack of observed data. The optimization method with total variation (TV) regularization can be used to address the ill-posed problems. However, TV regularization is susceptible to the staircase effect, which blurs the edges. In order to alleviate the staircase effect, in this study, the <tex>$\boldsymbol{\mathrm{L}^{\mathrm{p}}}$</tex> -norm TV as the regularization factor is applied to the subspace-based optimization method, and parameter p is adaptively adjusted to the gradient of the image. It can not only avoid the staircase effect but also eliminate noise in measured scattering data. Numerical experiments prove that the method not only has good reliability but also preserves the local feature of the object.

articleTitle: Dynamic modelling of uncertain multiple coupled delays complex networks and its robust adaptive tracking control
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In this letter, we model a class of uncertain multiple coupled delays complex networks. The robust tracking control of the uncertain multiple coupled delays complex networks is studied in depth. During the theory of pinning control technique, Lyapunov stability theory and adaptive control methode, we design the adaptive feedback tracking controllers and adaptive pinning feedback tracking controllers for the uncertain complex dynamical networks, respectively. Finally, numerical examples verify the correctness of the obtained results.

Author Keywords: uncertain multiple coupled delays complex networks

articleTitle: A Channel Attention based Large Kernel Convolutional Neural Network for Bearing Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: We propose an improved end-to-end Channel Attention based Large Kernel Convolutional Neural Network (CALKCNN) in this paper. The CALKCNN can automatically extract features from the original vibration signal and accurately diagnose bearing fault without any manual feature selection operations. We break the stereotype and innovatively use a large kernel in the first layer of CALKCNN to extract the long-time scale characteristics and suppress high-frequency noise, which improves the anti-noise and generalization ability. The CALKCNN can adaptively adjust the weights of feature maps generated by large kernel convolutions based on the channel attention mechanism, selectively focus on essential features and ignore unimportant features, which improves the adaptability and robustness. Compared with five excellent baseline models, the CALKCNN achieves state-of-the-art performance in bearing fault diagnosis by experiments using CWRU bearing fault dataset.

articleTitle: Machine Translation Based on Syntactic Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Machine translation refers to the process of translating source language sentences into semantically equivalent target language sentences through computers, and is an important research direction in the field of natural language processing. Neural machine translation only needs to use neural networks to achieve end-to-end translation from source language to target language, which has become the mainstream direction of machine translation research. There are also some problems such as fluent but not faithful translation, difficulty in processing rare words, poor performance of low-resource languages, poor cross-domain adaptability, and low utilization of prior knowledge. Inspired by the research of statistical machine translation, it has become a hot topic in the field of neural machine translation to integrate linguistic information into the neural machine translation model and utilize the existing linguistic knowledge to alleviate the inherent difficulties faced by neural machine translation and improve the translation quality. According to the classification system of grammatical units, researches in this field can be divided into three categories: neural machine translation (NMT) integrating word structure information, neural machine translation integrating phrase structure information and neural machine translation integrating syntactic structure information. Current researches also focus on these three aspects. Firstly, the challenges and causes of neural machine translation are described, and then the research status and main results of neural machine translation based on language knowledge are introduced. At last, the questions in existing research are summarized, and the future research direction is prospected.

articleTitle: Intelligent Safe Driving Assistance System Based On Improved YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The car accident caused by driver's violation behaviors has always been one of the biggest dangers that threaten the safety of human life and property. In order to reduce the occurrence of car accidents, vehicle-mounted assistance driving systems have emerged as the times require. However, the cost of assistance driving systems in the current market is relatively high, and they only appear in high-end car brands, leaving gaps in the mid-to-low-end market. Starting from the low cost and reliability, this paper designs a set of assistance driving system to intelligently detect and warn the driver's violation behavior. The vision algorithm of the system is YOLOv5 optimized through attention mechanism and edge detection, and it's deployed on Jetson Xavier NX to ensure data security and model robustness. The algorithm combines hardware equipment, client, back-end server and Hadoop big data technology to realize the functions of drunk driving detection, intelligent monitoring of driver behavior and early warning. The solution proposed in this paper uses self-optimized open-source vision algorithms, and the main expenses come from the procurement, development of hardware equipment and cloud service. The cost is low, and it provides the possibility for the introduction of assisted driving systems in the low-end automobile market. After actual testing, the system is low in cost, easy to maintain, and at the same time meets the requirements of accuracy and real-time performance, ensuring the safety of drivers and passengers during driving.

articleTitle: Highly overlapping strawberry leaf detection based on YOLOv5s-MBLS deep learning method
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In response to the existing object detection algorithms are applied to complex strawberry planting scenes with poor detection accuracy, slow speed and difficult deployment, this paper proposes a lightweight YOLOv5s-MBLS detection algorithm. First of all, replace the CBS module in the YOLOv5 backbone network with the MBL module. The multi-scale convolution kernel of the MBL module can enhance the feature extraction ability of the backbone network while reducing the amounts of parameters and model size. Secondly, SIoU loss function is used to improve model accuracy and model detection speed. Finally, compared with the current popular target detection algorithm, the experimental results show that the the mean average precision (mAP) of YOLOv5s-MBLS algorithm is 1.6% higher than the original algorithm, the model size is reduced by 21.9%, and the average detection speed of each image is only 5.19 ms. Even compared with the latest YOLOv7, the mAP of YOLOv5s-MBLS is also improved by 0.4%, and other indicators are also better than YOLOv7, which proves the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: A Survey of Vehicle Trajectory Prediction Based on Deep-Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Trajectory prediction is very important for autonomous driving vehicles. Deep-learning approaches can capture the interaction information. Therefore more and more researchers are using deep-learning models to accomplish vehicle trajectory prediction. This paper provides a detailed and comparative description of the methods for vehicle trajectory prediction based on deep-learning models. We start by modelling trajectory predictions for vehicles. Several common deep-learning models used in vehicle trajectory prediction are then highlighted. Next, we compare the structural features, salient advantages and applicable scenarios of commonly used deep-learning models. Future directions for vehicle trajectory prediction are discussed at the end.

articleTitle: BERTGACN: Text Classification by Combining BERT and GCN and GAT
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: With the explosive growth of electronic data, text has become one of the most important information carriers, and it has become the most common form of data display. Text classification involves many fields such as artificial intelligence and pattern recognition, so it has important academic research significance and commercial value. How to make the computer accurately locate the effective information in the text and realize automatic classification has become one of the research hotspots. In this study, we propose the BERTGACN model, which combines the large-scale pre-training model and the double-tower structure Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) model for text classification tasks. The BERTGACN model creates a heterogeneous graph for representing documents and words as nodes, respectively. By jointly training the Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) module, Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) module and Graph Attention Network (GAT) module, the BERTGACN model effectively learns the structural information of the graph and the association information between nodes, which enhances its text classification ability. Experiments show that the BERTGACN model achieves better results than previous models in a wide range of text classification tasks.

articleTitle: Human Segmentation Using Commercial Wi-Fi Device
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Image segmentation technology is widely used in automatic driving, smart home and other fields. However, due to the problem of privacy of image methods, they face restrictions when used in private occasions. In order to avoiding private problem image-based method, we proposed a human segmentation method based on commercial Wi-Fi devices named Wi-Seg, which is used to extract human silhouette information and generate pixel-level annotations. So that it can be integrated with existing human- computer interaction schemes using image segmentation, and avoiding the privacy problem of image segmentation methods. In this paper, the channel state index (CSI) in the Wi-Fi signal is collected as the original data, and a encoder-decoder deep neural network is designed to extract the human silhouette information from the CSI signal. Compared with the mainstream image segmentation methods, our Wi-Seg is superior to recent work that using Wi-Fi signal to extract human silhouette information, and performs as well as image segmentation methods.

articleTitle: Research on hybrid multiple hypothesis prediction reconstruction algorithm based on measured value reorganization
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Focusing on the MH-BCS-SPL framework, aiming at the problem that the theoretical conditions of the multi-hypothesis prediction algorithm can not be satisfied with high probability in the case of low sampling rate, resulting in poor reconstruction quality, a hybrid multi-hypothesis prediction reconstruction algorithm based on measurement value reorganization is proposed. On the basis of this algorithm, in order to prevent the negative impact of inaccurate edge information on the reconstruction quality, a mixed multiple hypothesis prediction reconstruction algorithm based on resampling is proposed. By measuring the similarity between the resampling measured value and the original measured value, multiple initial reconstruction results are adaptively mixed to obtain the final reconstruction results. Experimental results show that the algorithm can effectively improve the reconstruction quality under low sampling rate.

articleTitle: SAR and Multispectral Image Fusion Based on Dual-Channel Hybrid Attention Block and Dilated Convolution
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The fundamental task of image fusion is to extract image features. Due to the difference in channel dimensions between SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar, SAR) images and Multi spectral (MS) images, it is difficult to fully extract and utilize the high frequency detail information of SAR images and the low frequency spectral information of MS images for existing algorithms to alleviate the detail loss and color distortion problems of fused images. This image fusion algorithm is based on two-channel hybrid attention and dilated convolution. Firstly, a two-channel network is used to extract high-frequency detail features and low-frequency spectral features of SAR and MS images, and then a dilated convolution is introduced to capture the image's context and channel context information, followed by mapping to the hybrid attention module for feature enhancement, and finally, the image is reconstructed by decoding network to fuse the images. And the loss function based on Spectral Angle Distance (SAD) is constructed, which can further alleviate the problems of spectral distortion and detail loss. Experiments show that the fusion network proposed in this paper has a more powerful feature extraction ability for images than other methods and is better than existing algorithms in subjective and objective evaluations.

articleTitle: Robust adaptive beamforming for antenna sensor array based on the reconstruction shrinkage method
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: An advanced interference plus noise covariance matrix (ICM) reconstruction approach was proposed to facilitate robust adaptive beamforming for antenna sensor arrays The proposed method involves the calculation of the eigenvectors and eigenvalues of the signal of interest (SOI) and the interference through eigen-projection processing. Following this, the covariance matrix without the required signal component is formed by amending the diagonal matrix of the eigenvalue Then, the mixed ICM is constructed using the shrinkage method. A quadratically constrained quadratic programming (QCQP) dilemma can be worked out to ascertain the difference between the proposed steering vector (SV) and the true vector. The benefit of the proposed method is that the ICM can be obtained on the move and also can be obtained more precisely in the situation of high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Finally, the results of the theoretical analysis and simulation demonstrate the robustness and efficacy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Disaster Remote Sensing Image Semantic Segmentation model with boundary constraints based on SegNeXt
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Semantic segmentation has achieved significant breakthroughs in many fields. However, there are still many problems in disaster remote sensing semantic segmentation. For example, there are boundary anomalies in the prediction results of densely distributed objects, and there are inevitably unreasonable results in the segmentation prediction. This paper proposes a SegNeXt-based network architecture with boundary constraints which combines a boundary module with output branch different from main branch, and improves the sampling layer of SegNeXt. The improved SegNeXt was tested on the FloodNet dataset, and the final model result, mIou, reached 67.2%, with an accuracy of 90.1%. The mIou was 2.1% higher than the unmodified SegNeXt. In addition, the segmented image shows that the model has solved the boundary anomaly to some extent.

articleTitle: Research on Image Super-resolution Restoration Algorithm Based on High Order Degradation Model
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Appropriate training of the design is crucial for real-world super-resolution Low-Quality (LQ) images, which are difficult to obtain matched High-Quality ground truth images (HQ), or realistic degraded LQ observations from synthetic photography. Most of the recent work is concerned with modelling degradation using artificial or estimated degradation parameters, but these metrics cannot model complex types of real-world degradation, leading to limited quality improvement. We have demonstrated excellent performance of the image Super-Resolution (SR) model based on deep convolutional neural networks in restoring basic High resolution (HR) images from Low resolution (LR) images obtained from pre-defined downscaling methods. It is generally believed that when the assumed degradation model departs from the single image sequence (SISR) method in the real image, it performs poorly. Other factors are considered in many degradation models, such as Blur, but they are still insufficient to cover the different degradations of real-world images. In the case of high order degradation, we introduce the synchronous design of the process of obtaining the core of the de-degradation pool and modeling the noise. In order to better simulate the deterioration of the complex real world, high-resolution learning gives a realistic picture.

articleTitle: Global Temperature Prediction by BiLSTM Model Based on Whale Optimization Algorithm and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: With the rapid development of deep learning, time series models based on neural networks have emerged at this stage, and the time series forecasting problem is one of the important research areas. Traditional time series models are only suitable for short-term forecasting and cannot achieve dynamic forecasting; while most neural network-based forecasting models have poor accuracy and stability for long-term forecasting. In this paper, we propose a bidirectional long short-term memory network (Bi-LSTM) prediction model based on whale optim-ization algorithm (WOA) and attention mechanism, and uses this model to study the global temperature change trend. Five evaluation indexes such as mean square error (MSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and goodness-of-fit <tex>$R^{2}$</tex> are selected and compared with the commonly used ARIMA model, and it is concluded that the index data of the model proposed in this paper are better than the traditional model, and the goodness-of-fit <tex>$R^{2}$</tex> can reach 0.92. From the prediction results, it is known that the global temperature will probably reach about <tex>$20^{\mathrm{o}}\mathrm{C}$</tex> by the end of the 21st century, which is similar to the predicted global average temperature of the World Meteorological Organization and international database is close to the predicted temperature, and the prediction is good.

articleTitle: PLA: Fast and Accurate Face Alignment Network based on Prior Landmarks
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a new method called Prior Landmark Algorithm (PLA) to address the limitations of traditional face landmark prediction techniques. PLA predicts the offset between real and prior landmarks to overcome the issue of solvable domain coverage and to handle different face poses and shapes. A new loss function with weights (PL-Loss) and the strategy of Online Hard Example Mining were also introduced to improve the accuracy of the model. The adoption of prior landmarks and an auxiliary classifier eliminate the need for face normalization during training. The results show that PLA achieved comparable accuracy to state-of-the-art models and had a small model size of only 10 MB with fast processing speed of 162 FPS on average.

articleTitle: Application of adaptive beamforming technology in underwater acoustic
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Beamforming technology is the core part of the underwater target location research. It is very important to study adaptive beamforming algorithm. Adaptive beamforming technology can not only effectively extract the desired target signal, but also form a null in the interference direction to suppress interference and noise, thereby reducing the output power of interference and noise, maximizing the signal to interference noise ratio of array output, and then improving the detection performance of sonar. However, in the actual beamforming environment, the performance of adaptive beamforming algorithm will be affected by steering vector error, sampling covariance matrix error and array response error. This paper studies the traditional methods of beamforming, introduces the methods to improve the robustness of adaptive beamforming algorithm, and briefly describes the application of adaptive beamforming algorithm in underwater acoustic array signal processing.

articleTitle: Missing Values Imputation Using Auto-associative Neural Network with Local Neighborhood Information
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Missing values of real-world datasets bring challenges to data mining. Popular methods for handling missing values are to replace missing values in a dataset using predicted values, called imputation, which is a fundamental task in many research fields. In this paper, we propose an auto-associative neural network with local neighborhood information for missing values imputation. Specifically, we introduce local neighborhood information into auto-associative neural network to make the spatial relationships among samples work. With the spread of neighbor information, the similarity of samples is used to supplement the missing attributes of incomplete samples, which facilitates network analysis of attributes associations. Besides, we propose a training method to iteratively update estimation by treating missing values as variables, in which the imputation error and the incomplete model inputs are continuously optimized during training. The training method allows incomplete samples to participate in the network training as well, enabling all known attributes to be useful. Experiments based on several public datasets validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research On The Selection And Calibration Algorithm Of Special Monitoring Camera
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: As an important medium for image processing technology to obtain original data for algorithm analysis, the camera is closely related to the accuracy of the algorithm. The first prerequisite to ensure the accuracy of the algorithm is the correct camera selection and stable installation position. Therefore, it is very necessary to establish a model that can calibrate the camera, and judge whether the installation position of the camera complies in real-time and match the camera selection guide, to make a strong guarantee for the accuracy of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on pavement marking recognition method based on MATLAB
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Pavement markings are an important part of traffic. Effective automatic identification of pavement markings can help traffic achieve efficient operation. In this paper, the median filtering method is adopted, and the window selects 5 * 5 template to de-noise the image, and then the image is enhanced with linear gray transform, which effectively improves the accuracy of automatic recognition of road markings. Design the Matlab GUI interface, add the main functions to the interface, and realize the automatic recognition of human-computer interactive pavement markings.

articleTitle: A New Approach in Discrete Event System by Deep Monte Carlo Tree Search
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The decision-making problem is one of core issues in discrete event system, which is often used to describe adversarial complex environment. Aiming at the problem that there exists huge space in this kind of environment, we use Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) as our main search algorithm. One of the key challenges is that, during simulation, it is difficult to accurately predict opponent agents' actions. To deal with this challenge, we propose a deep neural network based on Long Short-Term Memory Network (LSTM), which is trained to predict most possible actions from opponent agents, the prediction is used to guide simulation. We test the performance of our method in the field of autonomous driving (AD), experiments are carried out on the simulation platform CARLA. We design a route containing several dangerous events. Results show that, if the prediction is accurate enough, algorithm using MCTS and deep learning outperforms the one using MCTS only, the former has a higher success rate in avoiding collisions, meanwhile it has a higher average speed.

articleTitle: Research on Gait Feature Fusion Method of OpenPose and GEI Based on Convolutional Network
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Gait recognition has the advantages of low resolution, easy acquisition but not easy to imitate, and difficult to camouflage, etc. It is one of the biometric recognition technologies with the most development potential at long distances. However, factors such as viewing angle, clothing, and walking with weights in gait data can make gait recognition performance poor. Convolutional neural network is one of the best deep learning techniques, which has the ability to fit features and extract typical features. Therefore, this paper proposes a gait recognition method based on a multi-layer convolutional neural network. This method is based on the OpenPose module to obtain the skeletal key point set of the human body in the gait cycle and the gait energy image (GEI) corresponding to the gait cycle, autonomously learn the characteristics of the target in a gait cycle, and use the triplet loss function to optimize the network. The recognition accuracy of the method above is 92.40% in a single view and 90.25% in a cross view after testing on typical gait dataset CASIA-B, which is robust to several uncertain factors.

articleTitle: Research on adaptive rate algorithm in bee colony ad hoc network
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive rate strategy based on lora, which reduces the influence of crosstalk during data transmission and solves the hidden terminal problem. Since the spread factor, bandwidth and coding rate of lora technology can achieve different transmission rates, the channel state is evaluated by calculating the received signal-to-noise ratio and signal strength of the rts control frame fed back by the receiving end, and the data transmission rate is determined according to the transmission rate threshold, so that the control frame and data frame can adopt different transmission rates, and finally realize rate adaptation. Finally, the adaptive algorithm is simulated on ns2, and the random topology scenario is used to verify the irrelevant characteristics between different working rate modes of nodes.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Abnormality Detection with Normalizing Flow and Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In anomaly detection, the limited number of abnormal samples results in a significant long-tail distribution in the data. Additionally, labeling is heavily dependent on the experience and can be time-consuming. This problem is particularly prominent in the field of abnormality detection from medical images. To this end, we propose a novel end-to-end unsupervised method for detecting abnormalities using a flow model-based neural network. Specifically, This approach utilizes deep neural networks to obtain the features of normal images and model the distribution with the statistical method. It maps image features to tractable distributions and effectively integrates both local and global relationships to identify distinctive features. Comprehensive experiments on the MURA dataset demonstrate that our method outperforms recent methods by a considerable margin.

articleTitle: An Integration method for calibration and positioning of space-based external radiation sources
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In order to complete the positioning of ground radiation sources by a single satellite and simplify the in-orbit phase calibration process, an integrated calibration position method based on phase interferometric direction finding is proposed for the space-based passive positioning of non-cooperative ground-based radiation sources. In the case of uncalibrated measurement system, according to the relative position variation rule of ground radiation source and satellite, the position ambiguity is solved by voting method and the phase offset is estimated at the same time. The simulation results of typical low-orbit satellite application scenarios show that the proposed algorithm can fast and quasi-real-time locate the target of stationary or low-speed moving external radiation source, and the accuracy can meet the requirements of on-orbit use.

articleTitle: Dam crack detection based on deep learning cascade detection algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In order to improve the crack detection accuracy of concrete dam surface, a cascade crack detection algorithm based on deep learning and prior information reinforcement is proposed. In the algorithm, two neural networks are cascaded to detect cracks by a cascade detection method. Prior information strengthening includes standardization and edge strengthening. When making standardized crack slices, the crack is rotated to the horizontal trend and the center of mass is placed in the section center. Meanwhile, slices belonging to the general background are removed according to the gray gradient similarity. The slices were processed with the prior information of crack edges to artificially highlight the features and reduce the difficulty of network training. The network results without prior information reinforcement and cascade detection are compared respectively to evaluate the network detection performance. The experimental results show that the accuracy rate and recall rate of concrete dam surface crack detection have been improved significantly, which proves the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Study on The Robustness of Cascade Failure and Recovery of Dependent Networks Under Load
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In view of the vulnerability of dependent networks and in order to avoid the huge impact of cascading failures on life, this paper adopts four dependent network recovery algorithms: random recovery (RR), preferential recovery based on local centrality (PRL), preferential recovery based on degree centrality (PRD), and preferential recovery based on connectivity link (PRCL). Using scale-free network (SF) and random network (ER) as sub-network models, a one-to-one dependent network is built with random coupling of SF-SF and ER-ER, and the cascade failure process includes dependent failure, overload failure and non-maximum connected network failure, and experiments were conducted to examine the recovery effects of these four recovery models on different recovery ratios and different dependent network models under the action of load [1]. In this paper, the curve of the robustness of dependent networks with load tolerance after cascading failure and recovery is drawn, and finally it is proved that the robustness of the dependent network after recovery is significantly improved compared with that before recovery, which proves that all four recovery methods are effective, and the relationship between robustness of dependent network after recovery and load tolerance, recovery ratio and edge parameters is obtained.

articleTitle: Dim-Light Instance Segmentation Based on Soft Thresholding and Improved BCNet
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Instance segmentation is a new method in the field of security monitoring. The current models perform well in sufficient light. However, in the actual environment, due to the change of light in the scene, the picture will randomly appear with high noise, low brightness and other problems which seriously affect the segmentation accuracy. Therefore, two S-BCNet based on BCNet are proposed in this paper, which respectively achieve better performance under complex light and constant dim-light conditions. In order to improve the generalization, we propose a new Shrinkage Module based on a soft thresholding function and insert it into BCNet's backbone so that it can learn and filter noise autonomously. Moreover, we propose a dim-light processing method and produce two datasets: COCO-D(dark light) and COCO-M(complex light) based on COCO, which are specifically used to train and test the performance of the mode in various degrees of dim-light environments. Furthermore, we use AdaBN to improve our S-BCNet and use the COCO-D for transfer learning to train the model for dark-light specialization, specifically for use in constant dim-light scenes. Experiments show that our models improve by 10.7% and 17.2% respectively compared with the best mainstream model in the two environments.

articleTitle: Global optimization using a combination of differential evolution and modified Powell method
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Optimization is one of the most important problems in engineering applications. Substantial algorithms have been proposed to tackle these problems, such as differential evolution(DE), which has excellent global search capability and robustness. However, like most metaheuristics, differential evolution is computationally expensive and difficult to converge to the exact global optimum. The modified Powell(MP) method is a derivative-free local optimization algorithm with fast convergence speed but is prone to fall into the local optimum trap. Combining the advantages of these two algorithms, we propose a hybrid optimization algorithm, which is called the DEMP algorithm. The DEMP algorithm is compared to other three well-known optimization algorithms by a set of benchmark functions. The results show that DEMP is not only notably better than the traditional DE Algorithm, but also highly competitive for other metaheuristic algorithms.

articleTitle: Long Text Multi-label Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In recent years, the evaluation of non-technical literacy such as sense of worth, outlook on life, and sustainable development concept, has become increasingly important in university education in China. They are often evaluated by questionnaires or interviews. However, the feedback texts from students often contain long paragraphs of students' opinion responses in Chinese, with long text, large amount of information and complex structure, which reduce the accuracy of long Chinese text classification. In this paper, we propose a multi-label classification model named MLformer, which uses the Longformer model to obtain feature representations containing information about the global semantic and local contextual features of the text to effectively classify students' views. The experimental results on our long text dataset in Chinese about engineering sustainability show that our method outperforms the typical deep learning classification model BERT in terms of accuracy, precision, and F1 score, thus, it can provide a powerful reference for students' opinion analysis and evaluation.

articleTitle: Dynamic Decision Boundaries for Improved Robustness against Adversarial Attacks
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Deep neural networks is vulnerable to adversarial attacks, where an attacker crafts input data to mislead the model. Adversarial training is a common approach to improve the robustness of deep neural networks against adversarial attacks, but existing methods mainly focus on maximizing the inter-class distance and minimizing the intra-class distance of adversarial examples at the feature level, as well as keeping them as far as possible from the decision boundary. However, these methods often rely on the assumption that the model has a determined decision boundary. In this work, we propose a novel method called Uncertainty Defender (UD) and based on uncertainty estimation to improve the robustness of deep neural networks against adversarial attacks. UD models the weight vector of the classifier as a Gaussian distribution and samples from it multiple times to obtain a dynamic decision boundary. Our experimental results on CIFAR10, MNIST and ImageNet show that our method performs well in both white-box and black-box attack scenarios.

articleTitle: A new appearance-based gaze estimation via multi-modal fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Appearance-based gaze estimation has gained more and more attention because of its generality, robustness, and subject independence. Deep learning, which has made a great deal of success in computer vision, has also greatly improved the accuracy of appearance-based gaze estimation. To further reduce the error in gaze estimation, we focus on extracting better feature information from eye and face images. In this paper, we propose a novel multimodal fusion gaze estimation model based on ConvNext and dilated convolution. In this model, the eye image and face image are used as input, and the ConvNext network is used to extract the features of the face image and the eye features are extracted by a dilated convolution-based network, and the feature map of the two images are fused using the fully connected layer to perform gaze estimation. In the experimental part, the designed model is verified on the public dataset MPIIGaze, and compared the proposed model with other gaze estimation models. The experimental results show that our proposed method has greatly improved the accuracy of gaze estimation on the MPIIGaze dataset compared to other related works. Our proposed multimodal fusion gaze estimation model achieves state-of-the-art result on the MPIIGaze dataset.

articleTitle: Effect of BDS-2 Different Orbiting Satellites on BDS-3 Single-frequency Single Point Positioning Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Since the BDS-3 started providing positioning, navigation and timing services to global users, to evaluate the effect of the different orbiting satellites of BDS-2 on the SPP performance of BDS-3, we combined the GEO, IGSO and MEO satellites of the BDS-2 constellation with the satellites of the BDS-3 in terms of the number of visible satellites, PDOP and SPP accuracy. The results show that the SPP performance of the BDS-2 IGSO satellites combined with BDS-3 was the best, the BDS-2 GEO combined with BDS-3 was the second and BDS-2 MEO combined with BDS-3 was the third. The horizontal and vertical accuracy of the BDS-2 GEO, IGSO and MEO satellites combined with BDS-3 respectively indicated that the combination of BDS-2 IGSO and BDS-3 mainly improved the horizontal accuracy, the combination of BDS-2 GEO and BDS-3 primarily improved the vertical accuracy, and the combination of BDS-2 MEO with BDS-3 improved both the horizontal and vertical accuracy.

articleTitle: Fault Location of Cabled Seafloor Observation Network Based on Fault Feature and Fault Distance Relation Mining Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Cabled seafloor observation networks (CSONs) have evolved over the last decade to provide abundant electric energy and data transmission to enable marine science. To ensure reliable operation of the CSONs, the technology for fault location with high speed and accuracy is essential. However, the existing methods for CSON fault location fail to deeply mine the relation between fault feature and fault distance, hence the location performance is relatively unsatisfactory. In this paper, we prove that there is relation between fault distance and transient current signal created by fault. Based on this, we propose a fault location method based on Fault feature and Fault distance Relation Mining, named FaRM. Firstly, we simulate CSON and acquire transient current signal by PSCAD. Then we employ variational mode decomposition (VMD) to mine the fault feature in the transient current signal. Finally, FaRM is proposed to exploit the mined fault feature to predict the fault distance. Experimental results demonstrate that the fault location performance of FaRM is better than the existing CSON fault location methods.

articleTitle: Research on Pulse Radar Jamming Recognition based on DE-SVDD
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: With the rapid development of modern electronic warfare, new jamming based on digital radio frequency memory forwarding emerge in an endless stream. In order to solve the problem that only known jamming can be distinguished, this paper proposes a pulsed radar jamming recognition based on DE-SVDD. The MobileNetV3 is used as the backbone feature extraction network. Then the features are sent to the DE-SVDD module based on the differential evolution algorithm to accept available classes and reject unknown classes, realizing the effective recognition of new class jamming under small samples. The simulation results show that the proposed method has an overall recognition rate of up to 98.3% for seven jamming, including three unknown jamming within the SNR of 0~10dB, and the recognition rate of known types reaches 99.79% under 8dB. The jamming recognition rate reached 91.33%, realizing the effective classification and recognition of unknown modulation methods.

articleTitle: Study on MRI Slices-based Lightweight Neural Network in Alzheimer's Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Currently, early detection and intervention are still the key to prevent the aggravation of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Computer assisted diagnosis can provide great help for the early detection of AD. However, compared with natural images, medical images are generally difficult to collect and always have small data sets. To solve this problem, we propose a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) slices-based lightweight neural network to effectively identify AD. In the proposed method, we use ShuffleNet as the backbone network for feature extraction. Efficient channel attention is added to capture the information of cross-channel interaction information. Triplet loss and cross entropy loss in deep metric learning are combined to ensure the multi-slices under the same subject are classified consistently. The experimental results indicate that, compare with state-of-the-art lightweight methods, our model achieves better classification performance with only 1.52M parameters and 5.56G FLOPs. Experiments verify that our method is helpful to reduce the number of parameters, FLOPs and improve the model performance. Through the construction of the model, it is expected to contribute to the improvement of AD intelligent detection on devices with limited computing power.

articleTitle: Neural Matrix Factorization Model Based On Latent Factor Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Aiming at the typical problem of predicting users' evaluation of items in recommender systems, we propose a neural matrix factorization model based on latent factor learning. Based on the classical latent factor model, the model utilizes the representation ability of deep learning, adds auxiliary features and cross features in the process of vectorization to improve the abstract expression ability of the model to the latent factor vector, and realizes the improvement of the model by auxiliary feature information. Finally, compared with the existing deep learning models, the prediction results are significantly improved in RMSE and MAE metrics.

articleTitle: Study on Applying Median Cancellation Adaptive Clutter Suppression Interference Algorithm to Airborne Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Clutter Suppression Interference (CSI) is a common radar signal processing method, which efficiently suppresses ground clutter interference in radar received echoes and can greatly improve the signal-to-noise ratio of airborne synthetic aperture radar ground motion target indication (SAR/GMTI). However, the implementation of the clutter suppression algorithm in engineering is difficult because of the large number of filtering power coefficients to be calculated in real time. Based on this research background, this paper models the ground clutter of airborne radar, analyzes the principles and performance of three clutter suppression algorithms, CSI, ACSI and median cancellation ACSI, and performs engineering implementation. From the engineering experimental results, it can be seen that all three algorithms can improve the airborne radar signal-to-noise ratio and thus improve the recognition capability of moving targets, among which the median pair cancellation ACSI algorithm has the lowest false alarm probability and the greatest performance improvement.

articleTitle: A Decentralized Data Crowdsourcing Framework: A Accountability and Confidentiality Perspective
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: An accountable and confidential data crowdsourcing framework comprised of the trusted execution environment (TEE), blockchain, and a distributed file storage system was proposed in this paper. To begin, participants may register using their true identity message, and only the guardians (or regulators) can securely review their registration information. Then, the requester submits and the executor republishes the crowdsourcing task con-fidentially. Following that, workers collect and share data via their smart devices' Trust Zone, and executors assemble, validate data in their Intel Software Guard Extensions (SGX). Furthermore, the data exchanged between participants is encrypted, and only au-thorized users can view them. According to the analysis and exten-sive experiments, our proposed system outperforms others especially in terms of latency, throughput, and task success rate.

articleTitle: An artificial bee colony algorithm improved by a search strategy based on adaptive selection
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of slow convergence and low accuracy of the basic Artificial Bee Colony algorithm, an adaptive selection strategy using population information is proposed in this paper. The search strategy is controlled by using the change rate of focusing distance, which not only ensures the utilization of the population information, but also improves the utilization of the best individual information by the algorithm. By comparing the improved algorithm with the basic algorithm through experiments, the results show that the improved algorithm has improved the search performance and convergence performance.

articleTitle: Research on Robotic High-Precision Target Detection Technology for Transmission Lines Based on Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In recent years, machine vision detection technology has been widely used in various fields, and deep learning, as an emerging visual detection technology, has shown excellent detection performance. In this paper, aiming at the bolt fastening end operation device of the live working robot on the transmission line, the visual detection algorithm is studied to improve the efficiency of the robot operation. In view of the poor robustness and high false detection rate of the visual detection algorithm designed by Hough and SVM, it is proposed to use the Faster R-CNN network with leading performance in deep learning to design the bolt detection algorithm. The size of bolts appearing in the camera is analyzed, and suitable RPN parameters are proposed. Aiming at the problem that the network model cannot be fitted due to insufficient samples, a sample expansion method is proposed to increase the number of samples. Finally, the bolt detection network is obtained through joint training. Experiments prove that the designed Faster R-CNN detection algorithm can effectively detect bolts, greatly improving the efficiency of robot operations, and has broad application prospects.

articleTitle: PENet: Pre-Enhanced Network for Object Detection and Instance Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Multi-level feature fusion has always been regarded as a powerful structure that can improve the performance of models for instance segmentation. In this work, we propose a novel proposal-based Pre-Enhanced Network (PENet) performing a bottom-up feature fusion between backbone and neck of the network, achieving a more adequate information propagation. Our main contribution is the new Pre-Enhanced Module (PEM) that utilizes feature maps generated by stages of backbone for multi-level fusion, which performs feature extraction and fusion on adjacent levels from bottom to top. Our PEM will equip feature maps with more sufficient information from the bottom, obtaining a more effective performance for object detection and instance segmentation. Evaluation and comparative experiments of models are conducted on Cityscapes dataset. Our PENet outperforms its baseline model obtaining absolute mAP gains of 1.3% for object detection and 0.9% for instance segmentation, and also achieves improvements compared with other corresponding models based on the same baseline. We hope our work will provide a new view of model structure modification for object detection and instance segmentation. Code will be made published.

articleTitle: Multi-terminal Service Access Method Based on Load Balancing
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Power communication service has obvious pooling and local correlation characteristics. Most of the traditional routing algorithms have poor adaptability to the structure characteristics and data flow characteristics of power communication network, and can not realize the reasonable allocation of network resources in practical application. This paper presents a multi-terminal service access method based on load balancing. A local communication QoS routing model based on multidimensional constraint mechanism is established, and a local communication network routing method based on load balancing is designed. Through comparative analysis of simulation experiments, it is verified that the proposed method can achieve load balancing, reduce the delay and packet loss rate, improve the utilization rate of communication link, and realize the priority arrangement of various access services.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Software and Hardware Cooperative Mode
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In daily work, there is a large number of remote document signing requirements. At present, the mainstream method is to mail the signed documents or transmit pictures of the signed documents. Obviously, mailing some confidential documents is not conducive to confidentiality, and the picture transmission of the signed documents is easy to leak and cannot guarantee the signature of the person. Combined with the above scenarios, a secure remote document signing solution is urgently needed in the current market. Based on the design idea of hardware and software collaboration,we introduce the domestic Hummingbird E203 processor with RISC- V architecture as the core controller, use FPGA (field-programmable gate array) to realize the convolutional neural network handwritten character recognition hardware accelerator and digital watermark embedding algorithm, and carry out functional simulation and experimental data collection.

articleTitle: High-Speed Tracking of Discriminative Correlation Filters Based on GPU
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Most existing high-speed trackers are based on generative models, which cannot distinguish between target and background. In contrast, the discriminative correlation filter (DCF) based on discriminative model treats tracking as a classification of background and target. To address the problem that DCF cannot track at high speed. In this paper, we propose a high-speed GPU-based parallel discriminative correlation filter (PDCF), decompose the DCF into parallel tasks and map them to GPU with different coarse-grained and multi-level memory. The experiments result show that PDCF is 58 times faster than DCF running on a single CPU with the same accuracy, and the speed is 2213 frames per second (FPS) when the patch size is 200*200pixel, which fully satisfies the task of high-speed tracking.

articleTitle: Cycling image encryption algorithm based on the new composite chaotic mapping
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In this paper, a new two-dimensional chaotic system (BTCS) that is based on composite of Bezier surface and trigonometric function is proposed. This system has large key space and demonstrates good chaotic behavior. In the meantime, using BTCS, a new encryption scheme (CIEA), named the Cycling image encryption algorithm, is proposed for encrypting numerous same-size images. The kernel of the scheme is that using the newly encrypted image encrypts a new image, circularly, which can improve security and is very efficient. Generation of pseudo-random matrices, scrambling based on matrix and XOR diffusion operation are included in each loop of CIEA. Security analyses and experiment results show that the CIEA performs well in key space, key sensitivity, histogram, information entropy, correlation analysis and anti-differential attack test.

Author Keywords: confusion operation based on sort index

articleTitle: Towards Graph Contrastive Learning for Recommendation with Sampling Embedding Perturbation
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Nowadays, graph collaborative filtering is the most practical and classical method for recommender systems, which learns user preferences through historical interactions between users and items. The recent combination of contrastive learning and recommender systems has led to a continuous improvement in the performance of graph collaborative filtering. A variety of data augmentation methods have also emerged. However, some graph augmentation methods are proven to lose graph information, such as the way of dropout on the graph structure. Inspired by different adversarial samples and different data augmentation methods, we adopt the method of adding interference patterns to the embedding space, as opposed to other models, we take a partial sampling of the embedding and then add the partially sampled data into the embedding, thus forming different sub-views. The extensive experimental results show that our experiments can improve the performance of the model more compared to other contrastive learning methods with our data enhancement method.

articleTitle: CMTR6D: Cross-Modal Transformer for 6D Pose Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: 6D pose estimation is widely used in robot grasping and autopilot. RGB image and point cloud are the two main data modalities, how to mine and make full use of the two kinds of data is the key problem. Some existing methods either deal with the two kinds of data separately and don't make good use of the two potential complementary characteristics, or simply splice the two features and don't make good use of the context information. Therefore, we propose a multimodal transformer framework Cross-Modal Transformer6D(CMTR6D). Specifically, CMTR6D includes a PointTransformer (PTR) branch, an ImageTransformer (ITR) branch, and a Cross-Modal Transformer (CMTR) module. ITR and PTR learn features from RGB images and point clouds, and can learn complementary information from another mode through the CMTR module, so that a better representation can be obtained. Our CMTR6D is 5.8% and 5.4% higher than the best method on YCB-Video and LineMOD datasets, and it also performs well in the occlusion experiments.

articleTitle: Salient Object Detection Based on Transformer and Multi-scale Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: It is difficult to learn global remote semantic information based on convolutional neural network, and it is difficult to obtain multi-scale feature information based on Vision Transformer, Swin Transformer and Pyramid Vision Transformer. However, salient objects maybe involve different scales. This paper introduces Shunted Transformer as the backbone network to extract multi-scale features to achieve salient object detection. Aiming at the problem of ignoring the difference between different features and dilution of high-level features when fusing high-level and low-level features, a decoder for progressive fusion of multi-scale features is designed. In addition, to solve the problem that the boundary features obtained may not match the salient object due to the separation of the boundary prediction structure and the salient object prediction branch, this paper refers to the BIG module and optimizes its feature input. Finally, the validity of the proposed model is verified by experiments on four widely used datasets.

articleTitle: Monotonic Optimization-based Resource Allocation for D2D-enabled MC-NOMA Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This letter investigates the joint subcarrier assignment and power allocation (JSAPA) problem in an uplink multicarrier non-orthogonal multiple access (MC-NOMA) hybrid device-to-device (D2D) and cellular networks. Considering the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) effects in the multicarrier network, our target is to maximize the sum data rate of D2D pairs subject to the constraints of the user power budget, power limitation on per-subcarrier, and the quality of service (QoS) requirement of each cellular user. To solve the non-convex JSAPA problem, we provide a polyblock algorithm by exploiting the hidden monotonic structure of objective functions and constraints to acquire the optimized result. Simulation results demonstrate our proposed scheme is better than the other methods.

articleTitle: ISAR Imaging Method for High-speed Spinning Targets based on Minimum Image Entropy Criterion and Compressed Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In accordance with the inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging problem of high-speed spinning targets under the phased array radar system, on the basis of analyzing the influence of the speed estimation error and sparse aperture on the echo resampling model, an ISAR imaging method of high-speed spinning targets based on minimum image entropy criterion and compressed sensing is proposed in this paper. Iterative optimization of the optimal sampling interval based on ISAR image entropy helps to eliminate the negative effects caused by the estimated error of spinning speed. Based on the sparsity of the resampled one-dimensional range profile, the measurement matrix is constructed, which is used to reconstruct the target ISAR images by compressed sensing algorithm. The experimental results indicate that the proposed method has strong adaptive compensation ability for different degrees of speed estimation error, and the reconstructed ISAR image maintains high similarity with the ideal result in conditions of different echo sparsity.

articleTitle: Research on power prediction of clean energy and operation optimization of clean energy supply system for typical regions
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: With the world energy shortage and the trend of global warming, the focus of energy is gradually shifting to clean energy. The promotion of clean energy represented by solar energy and wind energy and the development of efficient energy supply system and operation have gradually become the focus of attention. However, when large-scale photovoltaic power generation is integrated into the grid, it is easy to cause the paralysis of the power system. At the same time, due to the lack of effective energy system operation strategy, it is easy to cause the problem of resource waste and low energy utilization in typical regional clean energy supply system. Based on this, this paper first proposed a short-term photovoltaic power prediction method based on LSTM according to the characteristics of strong timing of photovoltaic power, predicted the irradiance data, and evaluated and compared the predicted effect. Then, a high-efficiency CCHP microgrid structure for typical areas is proposed, and the operation strategy of this system is optimized based on particle swarm algorithm. The experimental results show that the proposed short-term photovoltaic power prediction method based on LSTM has higher prediction accuracy than other prediction methods. At the same time, the micro-grid structure and the operation strategy of the design proposed in this paper have high economy, thus verifying the advanced nature of the work in this paper.

articleTitle: Monintoring Student Depression by Mobile Devices with Autoencoder Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The timely assessment of mental health is difficult since we lack the objective measurements of symptoms, especially for the Covid-19 pandemic quarantined students. Fortunately, smart phones can capture the real-world data such as the GPS traces and the phone active time et.al that link the behavioral patterns to the mental health. However, recent studies are based on a very small size of participants and only collect fewer phone features, which means that the effective predicting models which require various features are hardly adopted. In this paper, we develop an android application to record multidimensional data of users as well as a PHQ-9 and a SAS questionary, and we distribute it to 176 college students to collect larger scale data when in quarantine period. To address the unprecise problem of handcrafted feature extraction, we design an autoencoder machine learning model to monitor the student mental health. Extensive experiments indicate that the performance of the proposed method improves its F-1 score for PHQ-9 and SAS by 5% and 6% to the state of the current studies, respectively.

articleTitle: Short-term PV Power Prediction Based on Bi-directional Gated Recurrent Unit Network and Adaptive Chirp Mode Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: With the increasing proportion of installed PV capacity and access to the system, accurate short-term PV power forecasting is critical to maintain safe and stable operation of grids containing a high proportion of PV power sources. In addition, a single prediction model has limited ability to improve the accuracy. To address the above issues, this paper proposes a short-term PV power prediction method based on bi-directional gated recursive unit (Bi-GRU) network and adaptive chirp modal decomposition (ACMD). First, to reduce the complexity of the historical PV power time series data, the ACMD algorithm is used for signal decomposition. Then a Bi-GRU network is built for the prediction of the sequences after noise reduction processing. The model is validated using actual power output data from a PV plant in Xinjiang, China. By comparing with SVM, ELM and BiGRU prediction models, it is verified that the ACMD-BiGRU model proposed in this paper has better results and can effectively improve the short-term PV power prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Defect Detection of Photovoltaic Panels Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The article proposes a high-precision algorithm for detecting defects in photovoltaic panels, which can detect and classify damaged areas in the images. The algorithm uses a parallel cross-encoding and decoding detection network, combining Transformer and convolutional models to extract and interactively transmit features, optimizing the calculation process and enhancing the network's perception of global and local features. Experimental tests show that the detection accuracy reaches 92.0%, which is far superior to similar detection networks.

articleTitle: Cascade Prediction with Recurrent Neural Networks and Diffusion Depth Distributions
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: A message suddenly in the spotlight can be an innocuous superstar scandal, but it can also be an extreme opinion that destabilizes society or a rumor that distorts the truth. Accurately predicting the future cascade size of information cascade on social networks such as Twitter and Weibo can help focus more attention on suspicious large-scale cascades in advance, assisting managers in making decisions for human intervention. However, early cascade prediction methods either rely on a priori stochastic process assumptions or handcrafted features, leading to limited prediction performance. Moreover, most existing deep learning-based cascade prediction methods use graph neural networks or graph representation learning techniques to model cascaded graphs of information propagation, which faces the dilemma of low graph embedding efficiency.
